A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, ICLR: In-Context Learning of Representations. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original graph-tracing experiments with Llama and Gemma models, representation analyses and causal interventions in Sections 3–5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains the original graph-tracing experiments, representation analyses and causal-intervention results, including Tables 1–2 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The graph-tracing procedures, activation averaging, PCA and Dirichlet-energy analyses, and representation interventions are unchanged. The Appendix B correction changes a formal constraint, not an experimental procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same square-grid, ring and hexagonal graph tasks, including the conflicting days-of-the-week semantic-prior scenario. No dataset, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The same one-shot and two-shot memorization comparators remain in Figures 5 and 20. Table 1 retains the same null and random intervention controls.

E3.justification: Model configurations, graph sizes, context windows, sampling procedures and evaluation metrics are unchanged. Appendix C.4 retains the same intervention design using 1,000 randomly generated contexts.

E4.justification: Appendix C retains the same layer-wise analyses, standardized-energy checks, causal interventions, spectral-embedding comparisons, semantic-prior experiments and graph-size scaling analyses.

E5.justification: Averaging descriptions and graphical uncertainty reporting are unchanged, including Appendix C.4 and Figures 8 and 19. No run-count, seed, confidence-interval or significance-testing information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Figures 1–20 and Tables 1–2 retain the same results and findings. For example, Table 2 reports the same grid PC/spectral-embedding similarities of 0.950 and 0.954 in both versions.

T1.justification: Theorem B.1, Equation (11), replaces the eigenvalue constraint λ_k(X) ≥ ε_k with the singular-value constraint σ_k(X) ≥ ε_k. This corrects a formal inconsistency for potentially rectangular X and aligns the constraint with the existing SVD proof; no new theorem or proof argument is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the same claims about context-induced representation reorganization, competition with semantic priors and the energy-minimization hypothesis.

C2.justification: The limitations on PCA interpretation and incomplete causal understanding move from v1 page 11 to v2 Appendix D with unchanged meaning. Interpretations of semantic priors, energy minimization and possible percolation dynamics also remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same batching and context-window details and A100/NDIF computational-resource information. No implementation details or code/data access information are added or revised.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning in Section 6 are unchanged. Publication details for Lee et al. (2024a) and Nanda et al. (2023), and the Nishi et al. (2024) author list, are updated without introducing different works.

P1.justification: v2 updates the publication header, funding acknowledgments and bibliography metadata, makes small wording and notation corrections in Appendix B, and moves the limitations paragraph into Appendix D. The research narrative is otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Publication headers change, bibliography entries reflow, and the limitations occupy a new final page. All figures and tables retain their arrangement, content, axes, legends and captions.

improvement.justification: Correcting Equation (11) removes an eigenvalue/singular-value inconsistency in Theorem B.1 and better aligns its statement with the existing proof. Bibliographic corrections provide additional editorial improvement. These gains are limited; experimental evidence, core claims and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
